blocks.text: The jewel inventory continues through rings, ornaments, gold vessels, and other luxury pieces that suggest the chest contains an entire courtly treasury. Dileram can barely finish naming the contents before desire outruns description and the value of the hoard begins to distort every judgment around it.

Hearing what lies inside, Maali Singh grew still greedier, until greed itself reads like the true subject of the page. What had begun as shared conquest now tempts him toward secrecy, private advantage, and a deliberate breach with the Ghanaiyas.

Unable to contain himself, he hurries to Jassa Singh with a proposal that the best treasure should be concealed rather than divided. The page closes on that conspiratorial turn, preparing the moral collapse that follows.
